title: Bay of Bengal Storm, Likely Named Arnab, to Hit Odisha-Andhra Coast on October 28
excerpt: The IMD expects the system to become a cyclonic storm by October 26 with gale winds gusting to 90 km/h, as Odisha puts 30 districts on alert targeting zero casualties.
body:
• A well-marked low over the Bay of Bengal is expected to become a deep depression on October 25 and a cyclonic storm — likely to be named Arnab — by the morning of October 26, the IMD said.
  • Landfall is expected on the morning of October 28 between the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts, with gale winds of 70-80 km/h gusting to 90 km/h from October 26.
  • Odisha has put all 30 districts on alert, cancelled leave for government staff in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri and Khurda, and placed NDRF and state rapid-action teams on standby, targeting zero casualties.
  • Fishermen have been told not to venture into the sea until October 29; diaspora families should expect disruption in coastal Odisha and north Andhra around October 27-28.

A low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by Monday morning and make landfall between the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts on the morning of October 28, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said, as Odisha activated its full cyclone machinery with a stated goal of zero casualties.

"It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a deep depression on October 25 and into a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by October 26 morning," IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said, in remarks reported by The Hindu. The storm would be named Arnab, a name proposed by Bangladesh, and would be the first cyclone to form over the Bay of Bengal in 2026, according to The Indian Express.

Winds and rain

Squally weather of 35-45 km/h gusting to 55 km/h is expected to strengthen to 45-55 km/h gusting to 65 km/h over the east-central Bay, and from the morning of October 26 gale winds of 70-80 km/h gusting to 90 km/h are forecast, increasing further until landfall. Very heavy rainfall is likely over coastal Odisha on October 26-27, with heavy rain continuing over Tamil Nadu, coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and coastal Karnataka under an active northeast monsoon. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea until October 29, and those at sea have been told to return immediately.

Odisha prepares

Odisha Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said the state's goal is "zero casualties," with all departments on alert. Leave has been cancelled for all government employees in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri and Khurda districts, collectors in 16 coastal and southern districts have been told to take precautionary measures, and district collectors may decide school and college closures. Cuttack's puja committees have been told to remove decorative bamboo Durga Puja structures immediately, trawler owners have been alerted, and the NDRF, Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force and Fire and Emergency Services are on standby. Extra attention is being given to Puri, Ganjam and Gajapati, where heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely.

What to watch

The IMD's next bulletins will narrow the landfall point and peak intensity, which decide the scale of evacuation from low-lying villages. For readers abroad: check family travel around October 27-28, expect rail and road disruption in coastal Odisha and north Andhra Pradesh, and follow district administration notices rather than forwarded messages for evacuation information.
nri_angle: Diaspora families with relatives in coastal Odisha and Andhra Pradesh should plan for disruption and evacuation notices around the October 28 landfall.
author: Diaspora Desk
